knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE,
                      fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)

A trajectory describes where an observation moves, while a buffer describes
environmental support around each position. A fishing operation can span
several neighbouring cells; a tagged animal's location and depth can also
be uncertain. **How do conditions around successive positions change along
the route?**

`extract_to_buffered_track()` combines the explicit trajectory assumptions
of [track extraction](extracting-environmental-data-along-tracks.html) with
the selection and statistics of [buffer extraction](extracting-and-weighting-buffer-data.html).
It returns every position and its buffer result, plus an optional track summary.

## Getting started: preparing our data

We reuse the real environmental subset from the point tutorial and a
fictional trajectory. Run from `vignettes/articles/`. No network is needed.

```{r setup}
library(ocean3d)
nc_file <- file.path("point-data", "temperature-points.nc")
source(file.path("buffer-data", "figures.R"))
track <- data.frame(
  lon = c(-0.10, 0.10), lat = c(37.98, 38.06),
  depth = 60, date = as.Date("2026-09-20"), recorded_temperature = 16
)
```

## Step 1: A buffer around each recorded position

```{r vertex-buffers}
observed <- extract_to_buffered_track(
  track, nc_file, var = "thetao", output_col = "temperature",
  horizontal_radius_km = 10, depth_radius_m = 10,
  infer_bounds = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
observed$samples[c("source_row", "lon", "lat", "temperature")]
observed$summary
```

The default uses only recorded vertices. Each value is the weighted mean
inside that position's buffer. The buffer combines horizontal area and
vertical thickness; it is not a sphere or ellipsoid around the point.
Time windows can also be added with `time_before`, `time_after` and
`buffer_time_unit`.

On axes without a buffer window, selection follows the point rules. A depth
method can be `nearest`, `surface` or `bottom`, while `2d` applies to a
variable without depth. `method = "all"` is unavailable here: each call uses
one buffer depth method. The buffer tutorial explains physical radii, cell
or layer index windows, and the explicit permission to infer missing bounds.

## Step 2: Explicit buffers along an assumed route

```{r route-buffers}
route <- extract_to_buffered_track(
  track, nc_file, var = "thetao", output_col = "temperature",
  spacing_km = 5, horizontal_radius_km = 10, depth_radius_m = 10,
  infer_bounds = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
route$samples[c("source_row", "is_interpolated", "distance_km", "temperature")]
```

`spacing_km = 5` requests balanced sampling with no more than five kilometres
between positions. The constant depth and date are retained. Changing depth
or time requires `interpolate_depth = TRUE` or `interpolate_time = TRUE`.
`time_step` and `time_unit` describe trajectory sampling; `buffer_time_unit`
describes the environmental time window around each position.

```{r buffer-route-map, fig.cap="Figure 1. Buffer means along an assumed route. White markers are recorded vertices. Colours represent buffer summaries, not point temperatures."}
plot_track_map(route$samples, observed$samples)
```

The line joins the requested buffer centres. It does not outline the buffers
or show where their winning environmental records are located. White markers
are the two supplied observations; the other positions were inserted explicitly.
Here colour represents a local mean, one result per buffer.
Differences between centres reflect different sets and weights of environmental
records in their neighbourhoods. The overlapping buffers can give similar means;
the function has not interpolated one mean into the next.

`sampling = "cells"` is also available, using the same grid intervals and
preserved observations as tracks. Here it defines buffer centres; because
the buffer moves continuously, a midpoint buffer represents its interval
approximately. It is not an exact integration of a moving buffer.

## Step 3: Two different sets of weights and coverage limits

`buffer_weighting = "weighted"` uses environmental area, thickness and
duration inside each buffer. `"equal"` gives its valid records equal weight.
`min_valid_fraction` determines how much of each buffer must have data.

`weighting = "distance"` then summarises the resulting sequence by travelled
distance. Alternatives are duration or equal sample weights, as explained
in the track tutorial. `track_min_valid_fraction` controls how much of the
requested trajectory must have a valid buffer result; its default is 0.8.
Rejected buffers remain part of that track denominator.

| Inside each local buffer | Along the sequence of buffer results |
|:--|:--|
| `statistic` selects mean, SD, SE, minimum, maximum or most similar. | `statistics` selects the requested track summaries. |
| `buffer_weighting` weights environmental records. | `weighting` weights positions along the route. |
| `min_valid_fraction` accepts or rejects a local result. | `track_min_valid_fraction` accepts or rejects a track summary. |

For example, we can extract local standard deviations and describe how those
standard deviations vary along the track:

```{r local-variability}
local_sd <- extract_to_buffered_track(
  track, nc_file, var = "thetao", output_col = "local_sd",
  spacing_km = 5, horizontal_radius_km = 10, depth_radius_m = 10,
  statistic = "sd", statistics = c("mean", "min", "max"),
  buffer_weighting = "weighted", weighting = "distance",
  min_valid_fraction = 0.8, track_min_valid_fraction = 0.8,
  infer_bounds = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
local_sd$samples[c("distance_km", "local_sd")]
local_sd$summary[c(
  "output_column", "valid_fraction", "mean", "min", "max", "variation_status"
)]
```

The final mean is the distance-weighted mean of local SD values. It is not
the mean temperature or an SD recomputed from the union of all model records.
Choose the two levels of statistics according to the question being asked.

The track summary's `variation_status` concerns `statistics`, not the local
`statistic`. Here it is `not_requested`: we requested mean, minimum and maximum
along the track, even though each local buffer returns an SD. Requesting track
SD/SE can give `available`, `insufficient_variation_samples` or `not_available`;
see the [track summary explanation](extracting-environmental-data-along-tracks.html#step-3-understanding-the-summary-weights).

Overlapping buffers can use the same netCDF records repeatedly. The track
mean describes the sequence of local conditions along the route, **not a
mean over the geographical union of all buffers**. SD and SE are descriptive;
overlapping buffers and adjacent positions are not independent replicates.

```{r buffer-diagnostics}
route$samples$temperature_match_info[[1]]
```

The diagnostic describes the actual buffer support and sources. The original
route coordinates remain the requested centres.

## Step 4: Selecting the value most similar to a recorded temperature

```{r similar-along-route}
similar <- extract_to_buffered_track(
  track, nc_file, var = "thetao", output_col = "temperature",
  spacing_km = 5, horizontal_radius_km = 10, depth_radius_m = 10,
  statistic = "most_similar", target_col = "recorded_temperature",
  infer_bounds = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
similar$samples[c("distance_km", "recorded_temperature", "temperature")]
similar$samples$temperature_match_info[[1]]$target_match$matches
similar$samples[c(
  "lon", "lat", "temperature_match_lon", "temperature_match_lat",
  "temperature_match_depth", "temperature_match_time"
)]
```

The match columns identify the winning model record independently of the
requested route coordinates. They are candidates for inspection, not revised
track positions. Unresolved location fields are `NA` and produce a warning;
all candidates remain in `target_match$matches`. Invalid connections also have
`NA` match coordinates. The buffer tutorial demonstrates the difference between
different-value ties and repeated identical values with multiple locations.

The constant target can be used at inserted positions without extra permission.
For different endpoint targets, interpolation needs its own explicit switch:

```{r changing-target}
changing <- track
changing$recorded_temperature <- c(15.8, 16.2)
changing_result <- extract_to_buffered_track(
  changing, nc_file, var = "thetao", output_col = "temperature",
  spacing_km = 5, horizontal_radius_km = 10, depth_radius_m = 10,
  statistic = "most_similar", target_col = "recorded_temperature",
  interpolate_target = TRUE, infer_bounds = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
changing_result$samples[c("is_interpolated", "recorded_temperature", "temperature")]
```

This assumes a linear target change between vertices; it does not invent
measurements. A missing target stays missing. `target_ties` and
`max_target_difference` have the same meaning as in the
[similar-value tutorial](extracting-and-weighting-buffer-data.html#selecting-values-similar-to-a-measurement).
Any valid buffer support is accepted by default for `most_similar`, while
track coverage still has its separate 80% default.

## Step 5: Exploring the selected values in three dimensions

Depth is the requested route depth. Colours show the selected value inside
each local buffer. The environmental record may have a different cell centre,
depth or timestamp; consult its `target_match$matches` to inspect those
locations. The figure does not relocate the trajectory to the winning cells.

```{r interactive-buffer-route, fig.cap="Figure 2. Assumed buffer-centre positions, coloured by the model value most similar to the target assigned at each position. Hover labels give the requested depth and time. The displayed line does not connect winning model-cell centres or show buffer boundaries."}
track_explorer(changing_result$samples)
```

In this example depth and date are constant, while the target changes from
15.8 to 16.2 degrees C. The colour gradient therefore reflects a different
target at each centre; it is not a reconstructed temperature field between
those positions. The display axes are scaled separately, so horizontal and
vertical lengths are not shown at the same physical scale.

### Route timing and buffer timing are separate choices

The following example inserts a position every two hours, while each local
buffer covers one day before and one day after its centre's timestamp:

```{r buffered-time-windows}
timed_track <- track
timed_track$date <- as.POSIXct(c(
  "2026-09-20 00:00:00", "2026-09-20 06:00:00"
), tz = "UTC")
time_buffers <- extract_to_buffered_track(
  timed_track, nc_file, var = "thetao", output_col = "temperature",
  sampling = "balanced", time_step = 2, time_unit = "hours",
  interpolate_time = TRUE, time_resolution = "daily",
  horizontal_radius_km = 10, depth_radius_m = 10,
  time_before = 1, time_after = 1, buffer_time_unit = "days",
  infer_bounds = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
time_buffers$samples[c("date", "temperature")]
time_buffers$samples$temperature_match_info[[1]]$requested$time_window_utc
```

The route has four positions including its endpoints. Each gets a 48-hour
environmental window; it does not get a two-hour window. The four windows
overlap, and changing the route sampling does not create hourly model records.
Month and year units follow the calendar rules explained in the track and
buffer tutorials.

## Step 6: Keeping marine-route assumptions visible

The polygon and raster mask options are shared with `extract_to_track()`.
They check the connecting route, not the locations of the winning buffer
records. An invalid or unknown connection retains its original observations
but contributes unavailable support to the summary. No automatic rerouting
is performed. See the track tutorial's island figure and executable mask
example before interpreting an assumed line as a marine route.

The returned `settings` records sampling choices and candidate source files.
It also has one row of sampling counts per track:

```{r buffer-sampling-counts}
route$settings$sampling_counts
route$summary[c("track_id", "n_observed", "n_assumed", "n_samples")]
```

`n_observed` counts original vertices; `n_assumed` counts inserted positions;
`n_samples` is the total, including positions with missing buffer results.
The settings table is available even with `statistics = NULL`. Summary counts
repeat for each output and should not be added across environmental variables.

The same four sampling modes as point tracks are supported. `vertices` uses
only supplied positions. `balanced` shares one subdivision across distance,
depth and elapsed-time limits. `merged_steps` combines distance/depth cuts
with temporal cuts and may produce close neighbours. `cells` uses grid-interval
midpoints. Calendar months and years retain their anchors; balanced sampling
subdivides each calendar span when necessary. The
[track tutorial](extracting-environmental-data-along-tracks.html#step-5-choosing-whether-to-interpolate-depth-and-time)
compares both step strategies with the same dive and explains the assumptions.
The sample diagnostics describe actual buffer selections. Inspect both:
one tells you what was requested, the other what the data supplied.

## Summary

We have described environmental conditions around positions along an assumed
trajectory, rather than querying only the cells crossed by its centre line.
Along the way, we have:

1. Prepared a route with the same sampling rules as point tracks.
2. Defined a horizontal, depth and time window around each position.
3. Distinguished weighting and coverage inside each buffer from weighting
   and coverage along the track.
4. Selected values similar to recorded temperatures and inspected their
   cell centres without relocating the original trajectory.
5. Made target, depth and time interpolation explicit, and retained the
   distinction between observed vertices and assumed positions.

The result contains `samples`, `summary` and `settings`. Each sample describes
one local buffer; track summaries describe the sequence of those results.
Overlapping buffers may reuse environmental records, so these summaries do
not represent a union of independent volumes. Marine masks check the assumed
connections; they do not infer a route or validate the winning cell locations.

### Next steps

- See [track extraction](extracting-environmental-data-along-tracks.html)
  to compare sampling modes, summary weights and marine masks.
- Use the [buffer tutorial](extracting-and-weighting-buffer-data.html)
  to explore support weighting, bounds, coverage and target ties in detail.
- Use [point extraction](extracting-environmental-data-at-points.html)
  when the question concerns recorded positions without surrounding buffers.

## Data sources and reproducibility

The examples use the same small real-data subset as the point tutorial:
**Mediterranean Sea Physics Reanalysis**, product `MEDSEA_MULTIYEAR_PHY_006_004`,
dataset `cmems_mod_med_phy-temp_my_4.2km_P1D-m_202511`, downloaded on
19 October 2026. The netCDF file is supplied in `point-data/`; no external
downloads or credentials are needed. Routes and target measurements are
fictional teaching inputs, while environmental temperatures are original
model values.

E.U. Copernicus Marine Service Information;
[doi:10.48670/mds-00375](https://doi.org/10.48670/mds-00375). Source data remain
subject to the [Copernicus Marine Service licence](https://marine.copernicus.eu/user-corner/service-commitments-and-licence).
The examples do not imply endorsement by Copernicus Marine or CMCC.

The [point tutorial](extracting-environmental-data-at-points.html#data-sources-and-reproducibility)
documents the subset and its preparation with `data-raw/point-article.R`.
Run this article with `vignettes/articles/` as the working directory;
`buffer-data/figures.R` supplies only display helpers. Environmental values,
buffer diagnostics and summaries are calculated by the public extraction
functions from the netCDF file.

## All arguments and defaults

<details open>
<summary>Expand or collapse the complete extract_to_buffered_track() signature</summary>

The signature is generated from the current function. Arguments without a
default require input. For vectors of choices, the first is the default;
supply one choice in a call. Track and buffer choices stay separate.

```{r buffered-track-signature, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
article_signature(extract_to_buffered_track, "extract_to_buffered_track")
```

| Decision | Choices, meaning and effective default |
|:--|:--|
| Data and grouping | `data` supplies vertices (a table or sf POINT features); `nc` supplies sources. `var = NULL` detects variables; `track_col = NULL` treats the input as one track, otherwise names its ID column. |
| `sampling` | `"vertices"` uses supplied observations; `"balanced"` shares subdivisions across all step limits; `"merged_steps"` retains separate distance/depth and time cuts; `"cells"` uses crossed grid-interval midpoints. Default: vertices; supplying a step with sampling omitted activates balanced. |
| Route steps and interpolation | `spacing_km`, `depth_step_m`, `time_step` default to NULL. Positive values bound horizontal, depth and temporal changes. `interpolate_depth`, `interpolate_time`, `interpolate_target` each default to FALSE; TRUE independently permits linear changes between vertices. |
| Time units | `"seconds"`, `"minutes"`, `"hours"`, `"days"` are elapsed units (days = 24 hours); `"months"` and `"years"` are whole UTC calendar shifts, clamped at month ends. `time_unit` defaults to `"hours"` for route steps; `buffer_time_unit` defaults to `"days"` for local windows. |
| Horizontal window | `horizontal_radius_km = 0` keeps point selection; a positive radius requests a circle. Alternatively, nonnegative integer `lon_cell_radius` / `lat_cell_radius` select neighbouring cells. Physical and index radii cannot be combined on that axis. |
| Depth and time windows | `depth_radius_m = 0` and `time_before = time_after = 0` keep point selection on those axes. Positive values extend the buffer; `depth_layer_radius` selects neighbouring layers instead of metres. At least one window must be positive. |
| `statistic` (inside a buffer) | `"mean"` averages values; `"sd"` describes spread; `"se"` reports the standard error; `"min"` / `"max"` return the lowest / highest value. `"most_similar"` selects the available value nearest the target. Default: `"mean"`; choose one. |
| `buffer_weighting` | `"weighted"` (default) weights intersecting area, layer thickness and temporal support; `"equal"` gives valid contributing records equal weight. This does not change which value is most similar. |
| `statistics` (along the track) | `"mean"` averages values; `"sd"` describes spread; `"se"` reports the standard error; `"min"` / `"max"` return the lowest / highest value. Default: `"mean"`; choose one or several, or NULL to omit track statistics. |
| Track `weighting` | `"distance"` weights represented route length (default); `"duration"` weights elapsed time; `"equal"` gives each supported sample equal weight. Distance and duration are separate alternatives. |
| Two coverage thresholds | `min_valid_fraction = NULL` resolves to 0 for most_similar (any positive valid support) or 0.8 otherwise. `track_min_valid_fraction = 0.8` applies separately along the route. Both accept fractions from 0 to 1; empty support gives NA. |
| `infer_bounds` | FALSE (default) requires available support bounds; TRUE permits documented inference from coordinate centres. |
| `method` | `"2d"` has no depth selection; `"nearest"` selects the closest valid layer to the requested depth; `"surface"` selects the physically shallowest layer; `"bottom"` selects the deepest valid layer. NULL (default) chooses per variable on unbuffered axes; `"all"` is unavailable. |
| Targets and difference limit | `target_col` names a numeric target column (or a named mapping by variable); `max_target_difference = NULL` imposes no extra limit, a nonnegative number limits absolute difference (0 requires equality). |
| `target_ties` | `"NA"` (default) returns NA with a warning for equally close different values; `"lower"` / `"higher"` choose the smaller / larger value. Repeated locations with the same winning value remain ambiguous; these choices do not pick a location. Most-similar coordinate columns are always returned; ambiguous fields are NA. |
| `time_resolution` | `"auto"` follows observation precision; `"datetime"` preserves instants; `"daily"`, `"monthly"`, `"yearly"` compare UTC calendar labels. Default: `"auto"`; `"custom"` is unavailable here. No temporal aggregation is performed. |
| Column names | `lon_col`, `lat_col`, `depth_col`, `date_col` default to lon, lat, depth, date; `output_col = NULL` chooses names automatically. |
| Distances and limits | Distances follow WGS84 ellipsoidal geodesics. `max_samples = 100000L` caps generated positions; `max_segment_km = NULL` and `max_gap_hours = NULL` disable connection limits until positive values are supplied. |
| Marine mask | `land_mask = NULL` skips connectivity checks; supply CRS-defined polygons or a single-layer raster. Polygon `mask_type = "land"` (default) marks land, `"marine"` marks sea; `mask_domain` defines known coverage. Raster `marine_values` lists numeric sea codes; NA / outside coverage are unknown. |
| Mask action and precision | `land_policy = "skip"` (default) marks invalid connections while retaining observations; `"error"` stops. `mask_step_km = 0.5` limits polyline segment length for checking geodesic curvature; it does not improve coastline resolution. |
| Diagnostics and messages | Buffer diagnostics are retained. `quiet = FALSE` (default) permits reports; TRUE hides ordinary reports while timezone and unresolved-location warnings remain active. |

Only these source and point-selection options are accepted through `...`:

```{r buffered-forwarded-defaults, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
forwarded <- c(
  "file_col", "lon_dim", "lat_dim", "depth_dim", "time_dim", "time_match",
  "max_time_diff", "spatial_match", "max_distance_km"
)
defaults <- formals(extract_to_point)[forwarded]
print(knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Argument = forwarded,
  Default = vapply(defaults, function(x) paste(deparse(x), collapse = " "),
                   character(1)),
  Meaning = article_selection_notes(forwarded)
)))
```

See [`extract_to_buffered_track()`](../reference/extract_to_buffered_track.html)
for units and restrictions. The linked track and buffer tutorials explain the
individual choices in their scientific context.

</details>
